SECOND URL: https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/10/25/israel-to-close-occupied-west-bank-crossings-as-hebron-lockdown-continues

THE FRIDAY COURT ORDER — STILL NOT RESOLVED. DO NOT FILL THE GAP.
Last night we reported a narrow Friday court order whose fate was unknown. After checking BBC (05:15 GMT today), Al Jazeera's 25 October Hebron piece, NBC, the Times of Israel live blog through 10:11 am Israel time, and Al Jazeera's 24 October explainer, I can confirm: NO approved source reports the order being upheld, lifted, extended or ruled on. Its fate is STILL UNKNOWN and should be reported as still unknown.
The ONLY new material is one named resident's allegation that it was simply ignored:
- Riyad Mureish, a 49-year-old Palestinian businessman whose home was demolished, told NBC: "A court decree was in place that should have prevented any demolition." He said soldiers proceeded despite his appeals: "They demolished and took me out by force." He also said: "No house, no land, no money, what can I do?"
This is a resident's account of a demolition carried out in defiance of a court decree. It is NOT court confirmation and NOT an official statement. Attribute it to him explicitly or leave it out.

DISPLACEMENT FIGURES — FOUR SOURCES, FOUR FRAMINGS (do not average, do not merge)
- ISRAEL KATZ, Israeli Defence Minister: "about 2,000" residents displaced by the operation. (BBC, 05:15 GMT today; Al Jazeera, 25 Oct)
- YOUSEF AL-JA'BARI, Mayor of Hebron: 2,200 people forced from their homes. (Al Jazeera, 25 Oct)
- B'TSELEM, Israeli human rights organisation: approximately 240 Palestinian families forced from their homes in the Jildah and 'Ein Deir Bahah neighbourhoods of Hebron on Friday and Saturday. (NBC, 20:00 GMT Sat)
- AL JAZEERA correspondents on the ground, 24 Oct: around 300 Palestinian families being displaced in the city's al-Jalda neighbourhood.
- PALESTINIAN AUTHORITY, in a statement on Saturday: more than 40,000 citizens forcibly displaced from their homes in the West Bank by settler violence and armed forces raids SINCE THE BEGINNING OF 2025 — a cumulative figure, not this operation.
Note that 240 families and ~2,000-2,200 people are broadly compatible at roughly nine people per household, so the Katz and B'Tselem figures are not necessarily in conflict; the al-Ja'bari 2,200 and Katz 2,000 are the two direct person-counts and they differ by 200.

WHAT "ESCALATES" CONSISTS OF, CONCRETELY
- All West Bank land crossings close on Tuesday, Israel's election day. (BBC and Al Jazeera)
- Palestinian workers barred from entering ALL settlements; per Al Jazeera, barred from most West Bank areas Sunday through Monday. BBC: most workers barred from settlements from Sunday, with the exception of industrial zones and a limited number of other areas.
- IDF wording: a "ban on the entry and exit of Palestinian workers throughout Judea and Samaria and the Jordan Valley, including industrial zones, as well as the closure of all land crossings" on Tuesday.
- Hebron, population 200,000, already cordoned off, movement heavily restricted. At least one whole street appears to have been flattened, per footage shared online. (BBC)
- Hundreds of homes raided in the Hebron area by Saturday morning and dozens of houses turned into military interrogation centres (Palestinian Prisoners' Society, via Al Jazeera).
- Around 70 people arrested between Friday and early Saturday, with hundreds more interrogated (Palestinian Prisoners' Society, via Al Jazeera). No updated arrest total is carried by any source I reached; B'Tselem says only that "Arrests and interrogations are also continuing."
- Raids in at least 15 towns in the northern West Bank including Nablus, Jenin, Tubas and Qalqilya (Al Jazeera correspondents).
- Before the 7 October 2023 attack, more than 100,000 Palestinian workers were permitted to enter Israel; only a small fraction have had permits restored since. (BBC)

NAMED QUOTES WITH EXACT ROLES
- ISRAEL KATZ, Israeli Defence Minister: "They will not be allowed to return to their neighbourhood until we've finished dealing with all the Hamas issues in Hebron." (Al Jazeera, 25 Oct) This is the single most significant new quote — it makes the displacement open-ended by ministerial decision.
- YOUSEF AL-JA'BARI, Mayor of Hebron: Hebron faces "a complete blockade"; the lockdown is "a form of collective punishment"; and the operation is "driven by the elections", with Netanyahu and his ministers attempting to secure the votes of the far right and the settlers. (Al Jazeera 25 Oct; NBC; BBC)
- BENJAMIN NETANYAHU, Israeli Prime Minister: "We will act to destroy this place, to change it completely." (Al Jazeera) And, in an i24 television interview released Saturday, he threatened a "very big surprise" for the Palestinian Authority. (BBC)
- MAYY EL SHEIKH, spokesperson for the UN Human Rights Office in the occupied Palestinian territory: Israel's move to lock down the West Bank marked "yet another episode in a never-ending stream of suffocating measures making life more and more unbearable for Palestinians."
- B'TSELEM: warned of Israeli "plans for collective punishment and acts that could constitute war crimes".
- BEZALEL SMOTRICH, Israeli Finance Minister, who also holds a post in the Ministry of Defence overseeing the West Bank and its settlements: called for the offensive to proceed "exactly like in Gaza".
- ITAMAR BEN-GVIR, Israeli National Security Minister: called for the Ramallah-based Palestinian Authority to be "dismantled".

OVERNIGHT SETTLER VIOLENCE, Times of Israel live blog (Israel on UTC+2 from today, so subtract 2 hours for GMT)
- 8:00 am Israel time = 06:00 GMT: settlers vandalised several Palestinian cars overnight in the village of Sinjil, near Ramallah.
- 8:06 am Israel time = 06:06 GMT, updated 10:06 am = 08:06 GMT: a Palestinian home in Jalud that had been taken over by settlers was set on fire during clashes between soldiers and settlers; Israeli forces removed Israeli civilians who were in a closed military zone "in violation of the law". The mayor said the house belongs to an East Jerusalem resident and had been taken over by settlers in recent months.
- Al Jazeera, Saturday morning: Israeli settlers stormed the villages of Yabrud and Al Mughayyir, east of Ramallah, to forcibly graze sheep on Palestinian agricultural land and damage crops (Wafa).
- The Palestinian Colonization and Wall Resistance Commission said on Thursday it had recorded 409 attacks by Israeli forces or settlers against Palestinian farmers, their land, olive trees and agricultural equipment so far during October.
